metadata.title: Marvell Stock's AI Bet Is Even Bigger Than You Think

content.text:
The chipmaker has gone quiet on its old, diversified businesses, making its high-stakes wager on AI infrastructure the only story that matters now.
If you listened to Marvell Technology (MRVL)'s latest earnings call, you heard an explosion of confidence. Management is now forecasting its data center business, the white-hot core of its AI story, to grow a staggering 50% this year and accelerate again to 55% growth next year. But the most telling number on the call was one that barely made a ripple: the 10% growth guided for everything else. That quiet gap is where you find the real story. Marvell's center of gravity has shifted so completely that the company you own today is a fundamentally different, more concentrated bet than it was just two years ago.
The Diversified Business That Faded From View
It wasn't long ago that a significant part of Marvell's story was about its broader portfolio. Management would spend time discussing the health of its non-data center segments, with executives noting just over a year and a half ago how they were "encouraged to see the recovery starting to gain momentum" in those other markets. The company even structurally consolidated the rest of its end markets, enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, consumer, and automotive/industrial, into a single new reporting category called "communications and other", a move that streamlined these legacy segments into one bucket, signaling their secondary role in Marvell's future.
A Pure-Play Wager On AI Infrastructure
What replaced it is a singular, relentless focus on AI. The data center business now accounts for 76% of Marvell's total revenue, pulling in $1.8 billion last quarter alone. This is the engine, and management is flooring the accelerator. They now expect the critical interconnect business to "grow more than 70% year over year" and are guiding for custom chip revenue to more than double next year. The narrative has been deliberately streamlined. Marvell's role has evolved beyond simply powering data infrastructure; it is now a key enabler of next-generation AI infrastructure. The old, diversified identity has been quietly shelved.
The Quiet Is A Sign Of Strength
This shift is profoundly reassuring. Rather than stumbling into a hot market, Marvell's management deliberately re-engineered the company to chase it, sidelining slower-growth assets to pour resources into the AI boom. The numbers confirm the strategy is working. The risk, however, is now one of concentration. With the old, diversified businesses fading into the background, the company's fortunes are almost entirely tied to the AI infrastructure buildout. For a deeper look at the company's strategic choices, you might find the analysis in Marvell Stock And The Multi-Year Bet Management Made insightful. The single most important thing to watch next quarter is whether management reiterates that 55% growth forecast for the data center business in fiscal 2028. That number is the justification for the entire pivot.
